one_line_contribution: A crossover identification design that separates 'memory's gain shrinks because the prompt got better' from 'memory's gain shrinks because the instruction already absorbed that specific information': two disjoint training halves each produce a bank and a GEPA-optimized instruction, and at a fixed instruction on fixed test instances the own-half bank (cells 6, 10) is compared against the other-half bank (cells 7, 9), so headroom and instruction identity are identical by construction and the own-vs-other difference Delta_info is attributable to shared training-episode information rather than to prompt quality.
closest_prior_work: Two, at different distances. (a) MIPROv2 (2406.11695) is the framing precedent a reviewer names first: it factorizes a prompt into instructions and bootstrapped demonstrations and ablates instruction-only vs demonstration-only on one training set, which is literally the two-container question. It does not threaten the core: its demonstrations are statically selected, not query-conditioned retrieval, it never holds episodes out across containers, and it reports no residual ratio, so it cannot produce Delta_info. (b) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) is the real threat: it already places ReasoningBank/Memento retrievers and GEPA on identical training trajectories across four domains and three backbones, which kills the 'nobody has put these in one table' framing (correctly withdrawn here) and pre-empts the motivation. The proposal's remaining delta rests entirely on the assertion that EvoAgentBench has no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching and no paired statistics -- an absence claim the authors admit they could not verify against the PDF. If any EvoAgentBench cell or appendix runs GEPA-instruction-plus-retrieved-bank, cells 5-10 become a seed-and-split refinement of a published table rather than a new result. The nearest measurement-object precedent, Experience Distillation (2607.21051, 'retains >=64.8% of the in-context gain'), already establishes the retention-ratio shape with weights as the second container; substituting an instruction for weights is an incremental move on that axis.
strongest_objection: The primary endpoint is very likely to be undefined or unreachable under the proposal's own pre-registered rules, and nothing in the gate structure prevents that. Prediction 1 demands Delta_info >= 3pt AND S_info >= 0.5 with the 90% CI excluding 0.2; since S_info = 1 - own/other, satisfying both requires mean(other) >= 6pt and mean(own) <= 3pt -- i.e. a held-out-half bank must still deliver a six-point gain on top of a GEPA-optimized instruction. But G1 gates the bank effect at I0 (>=6pt paired, lower 80% CI >=3pt), not at I1, and every result the proposal itself cites predicts the I1-side number will be far smaller: the program's own pilot found the ExpeL bank TOST-equivalent to zero on Qwen3.5-27B (+0.6pt, 90% CI [-1.2, +2.5]) and a one-line instruction dominating every memory manipulation; EvoMemBench, MemHarness (70.1 vs 76.4 on ALFWorld) and the headroom logic all point the same way. The modal outcome is therefore g(I1a, B_b) in the 1-4pt band, where the proposal's own branch says S_info is 'undefined and Delta_info alone is reported' and where the pre-registered 3pt claim threshold sits at or above the effect itself. The paper then consists of outcome (i) -- 'the drop is headroom, the un-optimized-prompt framing is withdrawn' -- which is the authors' own stated most-likely death, plus a descriptive retrieval/compile/dump ladder. That is an honest null, but a reviewer will ask what the ICLR contribution is when the identification arm the whole design is built around returns 'inconclusive', and will note that the design bought a 44,000-episode primary grid to answer a question it gated in the wrong place. Compounding this: SE(Delta_info) ~= 0.7pt is optimistic, because all eight contrasts (4 seeds x 2 directions) run on the same 1000 instances, so instance-level discordance (which the proposal's own arithmetic puts at ~1.1-1.3pt for a single contrast) does not average down by sqrt(8) under a cluster bootstrap that resamples instances.
what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes, roughly in order of importance. (1) Move the gate to where the endpoint lives: add a pre-registered S_dev gate requiring g(I1a(s), B_b) -- memory gain at an already-optimized instruction from a bank the optimizer never saw -- to clear roughly 6pt, not just G1's 6pt at I0. If that fails on S_dev, the study should be re-framed before S_test is touched as the headroom paper (the honest and still-publishable version: 'a memory bank's headline delta is measured at a prompt with headroom, and here is exactly how much of it survives an optimizer'), with the ladder and coupling cells as the body, rather than discovering that after 44,000 episodes. (2) Add the union-half instruction I1_{a+b} as a Tier 0 cell (see missing_baseline). (3) De-risk the 'this is a property of GEPA plus one distiller prompt' reading by promoting the MIPROv2 optimizer arm and D_opt out of Tier 2 -- as written they are the last things run and the first things cut, yet prediction 9 and refutation (iii) both depend on them; a S_info that is reported for exactly one optimizer, one reflector (Claude) and one distiller prompt is a measurement of two prompts the authors wrote, and the two-bank-format check does not cover the instruction side. (4) Reconsider E1: BM25 multi-hop QA is a poor place to look for procedural experience value (the reusable lesson is roughly 'decompose and cite'), while E2/ALFWorld is the maximally template-repetitive case where a compiled block is nearly guaranteed to tie retrieval -- so prediction 4 is close to unfalsifiable there. A tool/web agent with recurring multi-step subroutines would make both the substitution and the compilation claims risky rather than pre-loaded. Separately, open the EvoAgentBench PDF before the design freeze, as promised.
missing_baseline: I1_{a+b}: a GEPA-optimized instruction trained on the union of both halves (all 800 episodes), evaluated with M0 and token-matched. The grid has I1a, I1b, I2a, I0, I_H, I3 and C_a but no instruction that was given the whole training set, even though that is the practitioner's actual alternative to a memory bank and the direct competitor to the paper's own deployment recommendation (cell 18, I1b x C_a). Without it the paper cannot answer the first question a reviewer will ask -- 'if I just run the optimizer on everything, do I need the bank at all?' -- and the compiled-block recommendation is compared only against instructions that each saw half the data, which structurally flatters C_a. Cost is small: one extra optimizer run set plus one 1000-instance cell, roughly 4 x 350 rollouts + 4,000 episodes, well under the Tier 2 budget already allocated to the gpt-oss-120b scale check. Second-order but also demandable: D_opt (the optimized static demonstration container) sits at Tier 2 and is fourth from the end of the cut order, yet refutation (iii) and any claim that 'compiled prose beats retrieval' explicitly require it -- a compile-wins result with D_opt unrun is exactly the 'prose beats exemplars' confound the authors say they want to exclude.
preprint_collision: Unusually strong in form, incomplete in exactly the place that matters. Credit where due: the check is dated (2026-09-03, prior scan 2026-08-21), reports its channels and volumes (15 HuggingFace queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 arXiv IDs, targeted web search), commits raw scan records, names the closest work, explicitly withdraws a novelty sentence from v2 ('no published work uses one as the control for the other'), reinstates five citations v2 wrongly retracted, and states a procedural rule for future retractions. That is far above the median submission and is the opposite of an unsearched novelty claim. The weakness is that the single paper the entire novelty delta rests on was never actually read: arXiv is unreachable from the node, so EvoAgentBench's (2607.05202) absence claim -- no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no paired statistics -- is inferred from an abstract, a project-page method list and search-surfaced descriptions of Table 3. Absence claims are the one kind of claim an abstract cannot support, and a combined GEPA-plus-bank cell is precisely the kind of thing that lives in an appendix or a robustness table. The same gap applies to 2608.14036's appendix, which the authors also flag. The residual-risk paragraph is honest (NeurIPS 2026 camera-readies in October; ICLR 2027 submissions not yet public; a 'GEPA + memory' ablation may exist in a systems-paper appendix) but does not discharge the problem. I also cannot independently verify any of the 2026-2027 identifiers cited here from my own knowledge, so my assessment of collision risk is conditional on the proposal's own reporting. Net: not a thin or vague check, and not a neutral either -- the novelty argument is currently load-bearing on an unopened PDF, and a reviewer is entitled to treat the delta as unestablished until that check is done.
